title: The Ceiling on What May Be Made Available Across the Benefit Year
content:
An allowance still owed to a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card is held at a ceiling for the benefit year, and which ceiling applies turns on the card's tier and on the standing of the medical plan that carries it.

**The rule.** The ceiling on the benefit year is the card's own tier yearly allowance, where the card's tier sets a yearly allowance and the medical plan carrying the card is in force; it is that yearly allowance reduced to the share of the year the medical plan was charged for, where the card's tier sets a yearly allowance and the medical plan carrying the card is no longer in force; and it is the allowance a benefit period carries in every other case.

**Which records decide it.** The medical plan carrying the card is the member's enrollment in the Medicare Advantage Health Plans, and whether it is in force is read from that enrollment's standing. The share of the year the medical plan was charged for is the count of premium charges raised on that enrollment over the 12 months to the day of the reckoning, taken against those 12 months.

| The card's tier and the medical plan | The ceiling on the benefit year |
|---|---|
| the tier sets a yearly allowance, and the medical plan is in force | the card's own tier yearly allowance |
| the tier sets a yearly allowance, and the medical plan is no longer in force | that yearly allowance multiplied by the months the plan was charged for and divided by 12 |
| any other case | the allowance a benefit period carries |

**Worked through on hypothetical figures.** A card whose tier sets a yearly allowance of 360.00 USD alongside a medical plan in force: the ceiling is 360.00 USD. The same card where the plan is no longer in force and 5 premium charges stand against it over the 12 months: the ceiling is 360.00 USD multiplied by 5 and divided by 12, that is 150.00 USD. A card whose tier sets no yearly allowance: the ceiling is the allowance a benefit period carries.
